To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synthetic peptides containing γ-COOH glutamic acid, which is a post-translational modification of certain proteins, bind calcium in the presence of magnesium.
synthetic peptides containing the γ-carboxy-glutamic acid (γ-gla) residues of protein C have Ca2+ binding constants and stoichiometries similar to those of the γ-gla-containing proteins.

the binding of Ca(2+) by the γ-carboxy-glutamate (gla) residues of protein C and other gla-containing proteins is characterized by the presence of multiple Ca(2+) binding sites with affinities ranging from 0.2 to 10 mM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the Ca2+-binding properties of various γ-glutamyl-containing peptides with counterpart sequences from human protein C.
the elucidation of the structure of the gla-containing proteins, and the elucidation of their role in the regulation of blood coagulation and other biological systems.
the elucidation of the binding of calcium to synthetic peptide containing γ-carboxylated glutamic acid (γ-gla) residues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ binding to the gla-containing peptide is a complex phenomenon.
the Ca2+ binding affinity of gla-containing peptides is directly related to the number of gla residues in the peptide.
gla-containing peptides bind Ca2+ with an affinity and stoichiometries that are similar to those observed in the gla domain of intact protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+ binding affinity of a given site is a function of both the local sequence and the overall conformational environment of the gla residues.
the gla domain of human protein C possesses 3–4 high-affinity Ca(2+) binding sites (Kd = 0.2–2.0 mM) and 5–10 low-affinity Ca2+-binding sites (Kd= 1–5 mM).

Ca2+ binds to the gla-containing peptides in a manner that is dependent upon both the length and sequence of the peptide and that the Ca2+ binding is not limited to the presence of only a single gla residue.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the binding stoichiometry of Ca2+ by gla-containing proteins is dependent on the length of the polypeptide chain, with the shortest peptides (e.g., FL(gla)(gl)LR) possessing a single Ca2+ binding site (n=1), while peptides of 38 residues and more have 3 or more Ca2+ sites.
the gla domain is a very effective Ca2+ binding site in proteins.
the gla residues of the gla domain of protein C are capable of binding Ca2+ with affinities and stoichiometries that mimic those of the gla region in prothrombin.
